title: The End Of Upward Mobility | NOEMA
gist: Branko Milanovic and Nils Gilman argue that the defining structural change in postwar capitalism is 'homoploutia' — roughly 3% of Americans who sit in the top decile of both labor and capital income — and that AI will end this arrangement either by entrenching it into a closed hereditary aristocracy or by dissolving the cognitive wage premium that holds it together. Either path destroys the meritocratic legitimacy story, leaving a pre-industrial pyramid of model owners, a thin elite remnant, a low-wage service class and a politically combustible redundant population.

insights.claim: Branko Milanovic coined 'homoploutia' for people who are simultaneously rich from labor income and from capital income, defined as sitting in the top decile by salary, by capital income and by total income; roughly 30% of the top American income decile qualifies, or about 3% of the total U.S. population.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Defines the actual marginal buyer of US risk assets: a household whose consumption and savings behavior is driven by salary and portfolio simultaneously, so equity drawdowns transmit far less to their spending than headline wealth stats imply.
insights.quote: We define the homoploutic class as those in the top decile by labor income (e.g., salary), capital income (e.g. interest and dividends) and total income, and we find that roughly 30% of the top American income decile qualifies
insights.locator: The Fusion & What It Created

insights.claim: The fused labor-and-capital rich class is described as the most important structural change in capitalism since World War II, and its share has risen steadily since the early 1980s, tracking almost exactly the rise in income inequality and the fall in intergenerational mobility.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Ties the 40-year inequality and mobility trends to a single identifiable cohort, so policies or technologies that hit that cohort's wage premium should move inequality metrics with unusual force.
insights.locator: The emergence of the homoploutic class is arguably the most important

insights.claim: A household drawing both a top-decile salary and top-decile investment income is effectively insulated from both the labor market and the stock market, because a bad year for equities is cushioned by the salary and a lost job is cushioned by the portfolio.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Explains why US consumption has stayed resilient through both layoff waves and market corrections — the shock absorber is diversification across factor income, not savings buffers.
insights.quote: A pure wage-earner is exposed to the labor market; a pure rentier is exposed to the stock market. The homoploutic household is exposed to both and therefore, in practice, to neither.
insights.locator: A pure wage-earner is exposed

insights.claim: Class struggle has not been resolved by one side winning but by relocating capital and labor inside the same person, which the authors call the only development in modern capitalism that would have surprised Marx.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Predicts weak political appetite for capital-unfriendly taxation while the fusion holds — and a sharp regime change in tax politics if AI severs the salary leg.
insights.quote: There is no class struggle in a household that draws from both factors — the struggle has been internalized and, thereby, essentially eliminated.
insights.locator: It doesn't resolve the conflict between capital and labor

insights.claim: In Mexico the fused labor-capital rich are below 1% of the population, and Brazil, Peru and Colombia follow the same classical pattern in which the rich do not work for a wage and well-paid doctors or lawyers do not own enough property to reach the top capital decile.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Latin American wealth is rentier-structured, so consumption of the local elite is tied to asset prices and FX rather than domestic wage cycles — a different beta than US luxury demand.
insights.locator: Compare this to Mexico, where the homoploutia sits below 1%

insights.claim: The fused labor-capital elite clusters at roughly 2-2.5% of the population in Spain, Italy, Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden, placing the United States at about 3% as the most extreme case among rich countries.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: The US is the leading indicator for a structure Europe is following at a lag, so US-specific political backlash dynamics should eventually show up in European equity and policy risk.
insights.locator: Richer countries fall in between

insights.claim: Sixty percent of American households have zero or negligible cash income from capital ownership, compared with 79% in Spain, 93% in Colombia and 96% in Peru as of 2021.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Asset-price-driven stimulus reaches at most 40% of US households directly, which caps the wealth-effect channel and raises the political salience of any AI-driven shift toward capital's income share.
insights.locator: Sixty percent of American households have zero or negligible

insights.claim: Capital income is roughly twice as unequally distributed as disposable income by Gini coefficient, and the top 1% of American capitalists received nearly $100,000 per person in capital income in 2022 — implying about $400,000 a year from financial assets alone for a household of four, from interest, dividends, rents and privately funded pensions.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Quantifies how much of the top 1%'s cash flow is already passive, setting the baseline against which any AI-driven rise in capital's income share compounds.
insights.locator: The top 1% of American capitalists received nearly $100,000

insights.claim: The fused labor-capital class proper earns about $20,548 per person in capital income, or north of $80,000 per family — not plutocratic money, but a solid income floor sitting beneath a high salary.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Sizes the passive-income cushion for the professional upper-middle class: enough to make job loss survivable, which changes labor-supply elasticity assumptions in white-collar layoff scenarios.
insights.locator: The homoploutic class proper — that is, people in the top decile

themes.theme: The merit ideology as legitimacy infrastructure

insights.claim: Daniel Markovits calculated in 'The Meritocracy Trap' that the parental investment gap separating an elite child from a middle-class child by the end of graduate school is equivalent to a traditional inheritance of roughly $10 million per child.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Prices elite education as a capital transfer, explaining the structural demand floor under private schooling, tutoring and credentialing businesses regardless of tuition inflation.
insights.quote: merit "an ideological conceit, constructed to launder a fundamentally unjust allocation of advantage."
insights.locator: In "The Meritocracy Trap(2019),"

insights.claim: Marx's M–C–M' circuit can be rewritten as M–E–M', where E is the education of one's children, and once that education becomes unreachable for anyone outside the elite, class mobility has effectively closed.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: A clean mental model for treating education spending as capital reinvestment rather than consumption — and for watching enrollment and tuition data as a mobility indicator.
insights.locator: One can put it as a modification of Marx's M–C–M'

insights.claim: The modern elite is unlike the 1960s technocratic class imagined by Tinbergen, Galbraith, Aron and Kerr because its material interest and its ideological commitment to private property are identical — it defends capital because it is capital and defends credentials because it is those too.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Predicts that the professional class will not split from capital on policy — undercutting theses that highly paid knowledge workers will support redistribution or anti-corporate regulation.
insights.locator: This isn't a technocratic class in the sense that scholars

insights.claim: The elite's political legitimacy for decades rested on a coherent offer — we are rich because we are useful, and you may join us if you are useful too — where the mere existence of a narrow and expensive path did most of the ideological work.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Identifies the specific variable whose disappearance triggers political instability: perceived entry, not measured inequality — so watch mobility perception surveys, not Gini levels.
insights.locator: That double grounding in educational credentials

themes.theme: What AI could break: entrenchment vs dissolution

insights.claim: The authors flag three open uncertainties about AI: whether it raises total labor output or merely shifts production from humans to machines without expanding output, whether capabilities keep progressing as promoters promise given circular financing of data centers and political backlash against building them, and how fast adoption translates into productivity gains.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Names circular data-center financing and siting backlash as the two concrete near-term failure modes for the AI capex cycle — both observable before productivity data arrives.
insights.quote: especially given the circular financing methods used for data centers and other computational capacity, and the political backlash against building them
insights.locator: We also don't know whether AI's capabilities will continue

insights.claim: Dictation software let people write faster without writing more because generating good ideas is the rate-limiting factor, changing the composition of effort without changing output — and the authors suggest something similar may hold for AI.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: A cheap test for AI productivity claims: if the binding constraint is idea generation rather than execution speed, seat-based AI pricing overshoots realizable value.
insights.locator: For example, dictating essays rather than typing them

insights.claim: The entire divergence between the two possible elite futures turns on one unresolved empirical question — whether AI is a substitute for or a complement to high-premium cognitive labor.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Reduces a sprawling AI-and-society debate to a single tradeable variable: professional-services wage premia and headcount, which can be tracked in law, consulting, finance and software compensation data.
insights.quote: whether AI will be a substitute for or a complement to high-premium cognitive labor
insights.locator: The difference between these two scenarios turns on

insights.claim: In the entrenchment scenario capital's share of national income rises because the quantity of capital rises with AI deployment while the average profit rate is held up by Schumpeterian destruction of the old capital stock, making the portfolio leg of elite income heavier.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: A mechanism for why AI capex need not crush returns on capital: obsolescence of incumbent assets keeps the average profit rate up even as the capital stock balloons — bearish for legacy asset owners, bullish for capital's aggregate share.
insights.quote: because the quantity of capital rises with AI deployment while the average profit rate is held up by Schumpeterian destruction of the old capital stock
insights.locator: As capital's share of national income rises

insights.claim: Under entrenchment the fused labor-capital class thickens from about a third of the top labor-income decile to half or two-thirds, and in the limit case the top 10% of labor-income earners become identical to the top 10% of capital-income earners, locking those positions in for their children as a hardworking aristocracy.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Quantifies a monitorable path: the overlap between top labor and top capital deciles is a measurable series that would confirm or reject the entrenchment scenario.
insights.locator: In this scenario, the homoploutic class thickens

insights.claim: Lawyers, financiers, consultants, software engineers and doctors command wage premia precisely for the credentialed cognitive work that large language models perform most convincingly, making them the group most exposed to substitution.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Names the specific labor cost pools AI attacks first — relevant for shorting labor-leveraged professional services and for the revenue case of vertical AI vendors.
insights.locator: Homoplouts typically work jobs that command a wage premium

insights.claim: Hans Moravec's observation that high-level reasoning is easier to automate than sensorimotor skills developed over a billion years of evolution implies the automation wave hits the credentialed elite before it hits manual trades.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Inverts the standard automation-risk ordering: wage compression should show up in white-collar cohorts first, while skilled trades retain pricing power.
insights.quote: high-level reasoning turns out to be easier to automate than sensorimotor skills developed over a billion years of evolution
insights.locator: As the roboticist Hans Moravec famously observed

insights.claim: If AI substitutes for knowledge work, the elite household reverts to a purely capitalist household living entirely off its investment portfolio — the classical Mexican pattern in which the rich do not work.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Implies rich-world elite income would become fully asset-price dependent, raising the political and market stakes of any equity drawdown and pushing capital toward yield and preservation over wage-linked risk.
insights.locator: The homoploutic household in this case reverts

insights.claim: Both AI scenarios destroy meritocratic legitimacy: under entrenchment there is no path of entry once inheritance is the only route into the top capital decile, and under dissolution there is no meritorious activity left to point at because one is simply an owner of capital.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Removes the hedge: there is no AI outcome in which the current legitimacy story survives, so elevated political risk is the base case in either branch.
insights.quote: In the first case the asset value of the class survives, but the flow into it stops. In the second, both go.
insights.locator: Modernization Theory Turned On Its Head?

themes.theme: The feudal pyramid and political combustion

insights.claim: The projected social structure has four tiers: a few thousand people who own the models at the summit, a closed elite remnant below them, a low-to-moderate-wage service class doing what AI cannot yet do (gardeners, home nursing aides, bartenders, tradesmen, mechanics), and a redundant population at the bottom.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: A demand map: mass-market and middle-tier consumer categories get squeezed while luxury and low-cost tiers grow — the barbell that already shows in consumer earnings.
insights.quote: At the summit we find the few thousand people who own the models.
insights.locator: Around this reduced elite the rest of society's structure

insights.claim: The word 'unemployed' is misleading for people displaced by AI because it implies a temporary state with a return path, whereas the redundant population consists of people whose skills are obsolete and whose retraining would take years that no one will fund.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: If displacement is permanent rather than cyclical, headline unemployment and participation data will understate the problem and fiscal transfer demands will be structural, not counter-cyclical.
insights.quote: the term "unemployed" is misleading, because it suggests a temporary state and a return path
insights.locator: And finally, at the bottom sits a redundant population

insights.claim: Universal basic income would in theory solve the material problem of the displaced, and more than a few in Silicon Valley dream of UBI plus TikTok memes as the modern update of bread and circuses — but the authors treat pacification as a political non-solution.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Flags UBI as the consensus elite fix while arguing it does not buy political stability — so do not price UBI adoption as a de-risking event for AI-exposed assets.
insights.quote: more than a few in Silicon Valley dream of UBI and TikTok memes as its modern update
insights.locator: In theory, a universal basic income

insights.claim: The emerging class pyramid is pre-industrial in shape — sharply graded at the top, flat and wide at the bottom, with no substantial middle — implying the 20th-century assumption that development produces a stabilizing middle class was an inference from an exceptional period.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Directly challenges the long-run assumption behind developed-market political risk premia: the middle class may be a historical anomaly rather than a durable equilibrium.
insights.locator: What is striking about this pyramid is its pre-industrial

insights.claim: If AI creates a rigid class pyramid, the richest and most technologically advanced societies may become politically more turbulent than poorer ones — a tragicomic inversion of modernization theory's belief in the universalization of stably democratic middle-class societies.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Argues developed-market political risk should be repriced upward relative to emerging markets — the opposite of how country risk is conventionally ranked.
insights.locator: If AI creates such a rigid class pyramid

insights.claim: A hierarchy that can be scaled, however improbably, is tolerable within a democracy while a closed-off hierarchy is not, which helps explain why many in Silicon Valley are moving in an explicitly anti-democratic direction, the subject of Gil Duran's 'The Nerd Reich.'
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Frames tech-elite anti-democratic politics as a rational response to closing mobility rather than ideology, implying it intensifies as mobility data worsens — a regulatory and reputational risk factor for large tech holdings.
insights.locator: A hierarchy that can be scaled, even improbably

insights.claim: The late Roman Republic fell not because the masses revolted spontaneously but because oligarchic clans could not settle disputes among themselves and each faction found it expedient to mobilize the idle urban population against its rivals.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Relocates the instability trigger from mass movements to elite infighting — so the signal to watch is billionaire-versus-billionaire political conflict, not protest volume.
insights.quote: It requires only that one plutocrat decide his interests are better served by mobilizing the malcontents rather than parleying with his peers.
insights.locator: The Roman analogy is relevant here

themes.theme: Burnham reread: who controls the instruments of production

insights.claim: James Burnham's 1941 'The Managerial Revolution' predicted that managers would take over the instruments of production from capitalists and that private property and its justifying ideology were headed for extinction, but by the 1980s America had reverted with a convert's enthusiasm to the sanctity of private property.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: A worked case study in how confidently a plausible structural forecast can fail — useful discipline when underwriting today's equally confident AI-transformation theses.
insights.quote: the sort of thing one cites to show how confidently intelligent people can misread their own moment
insights.locator: In April 1941, with the Wehrmacht in Paris

insights.claim: Managers did rise but rose into capital rather than against it, becoming capitalists themselves and producing a ruling class simultaneously at the top of the wage distribution and the ownership distribution — an outcome neither Burnham nor Marx anticipated.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Explains equity-based executive compensation as the mechanism that aligned management with capital — and why governance reform aimed at splitting the two keeps failing.
insights.locator: The managers did rise. But they didn't rise against capital

insights.claim: The shareholder value revolution of the 1970s-1980s dethroned the postwar managerial class and ensured corporations would place the interests of capital ahead of all other stakeholders, which is why Burnham predicted the wrong political outcome.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Dates the regime that current buyback-and-margin norms rest on, and implies those norms are contingent political settlements rather than permanent features.
insights.locator: Burnham's Question, Again

insights.claim: Enlisting Burnham in arguments about a 'woke' professional-managerial class is a misunderstanding or misappropriation, because he wrote about people who control the machines, not about the opinions of the credentialed.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Redirects attention from culture-war framing toward the ownership question — who owns the compute and models — as the analytically load-bearing variable.
insights.quote: He was writing about the people who control the machines.
insights.locator: which is why the recent enthusiasm for enlisting him

insights.claim: If artificial intelligence becomes the decisive instrument of modern production, then those who control it become the new ruling class and educational credentials will no longer legitimate the socioeconomic hierarchy.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Concentration of model and compute ownership becomes the single highest-stakes structural variable — a case for watching who holds frontier model equity rather than who holds application-layer revenue.
insights.locator: Applied to our moment, his question

insights.claim: The current elite may be the last generation of a ruling class required to be good at something other than clipping coupons, and the roughly 40-year settlement in which the same people held the best jobs and the most property — citing the first to justify the second — is ending one way or another.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: The authors' one high-conviction call: regime change in the elite income structure is certain even though its direction is not, so position for volatility in labor-vs-capital policy rather than for a specific outcome.
insights.quote: The homoplouts may end up being the last generation of a ruling class that was required to be good at something other than clipping coupons.
insights.locator: Burnham's Question, Again

insights.claim: Advocates of abundance who imagine machines doing the work while humans enjoy leisure have described the economics correctly and the politics not at all — abundance may well arrive without a society organized in a way anyone outside the ultra-elite would want.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Separates the productivity thesis from the political outcome: an AI bull case on output can coexist with a bear case on institutional stability, which is how to hedge the trade.
insights.quote: We may well get abundance. But what we won't get on present trajectories is a society organized in a way that anyone outside of the ultra-elite would want.
insights.locator: Advocates of abundance who imagine machines
